messages:
alex_support: Hey, heads up — enterprise-cust-42 is seeing a big auth spike and token failures from EU users starting ~08:10UTC. They claim latency went from ~60ms to 1.2s and many requests 401. Billing shows token retries. Can we triage?

maria_sre: Oof. Any evidence they hit the wrong region?

alex_support: Customer sent curl + dig. curl shows response headers: x-region: sin (APAC) even though users in DE. Dig output shows answer from apac-edge.example.net cname -> loadbalancer.apac.

alex_support: paste: ```
$ dig +short @8.8.8.8 api.example.com A
192.0.2.11
api.example.com. 180 IN CNAME apac-edge.example.net.
```

devon_net: Can you paste the HTTP header? need to confirm which backend signed the token.

alex_support: ```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 08:12:03 GMT
Server: redwood-edge
X-Region: ap-sin-1
X-Auth-Backend: token-svc-v3
```

maria_sre: That X-Region header means request landed in APAC pool. Two likely causes: GeoIP DB stale OR resolver/ISP returning cached apac answer. Did they recently rotate the CNAME?

kai_eng: We rolled a small CNAME rotation for weight testing last night (canary -> apac). TTLs were 300s but I thought we invalidated. Checking rollout logs...

deploy-bot: canary-rollout: CNAME api.example.com -> apac-edge applied at 2026-03-10T07:05:00Z to 10% of traffic.

kai_eng: Ah — rollout was to 10% for 1h, then supposed to revert, but revert step failed for certain delegations. Looks like some resolvers still holding the apac CNAME because of older TTL and upstream ISP caching.

devon_net: Also check EDNS-Client-Subnet behavior. Some ISPs ignore ECS and return a single apac answer for EU clients. That would cause cross-region routing but not explain 401s unless token backend is regional.

maria_sre: Token signing service is regional and rejects tokens issued in EU pool if validated in APAC — hence 401. So mismatch between where token issued and where request validated.

tony_pm: Customer impact: retries trigger billing bump and high latency. They want immediate mitigation and a mitigation plan.

alex_support: For immediate mitigation I suggested: 1) add short-term routing rule to prefer eu-pop answers at our edge router for their org-id, 2) ask them to flush any DNS on their app side, 3) temporary rollback of canary CNAME. Thoughts?

maria_sre: Agreed. Quick fix: purge the apac CNAME from our authoritative cache and revert the canary. Also push a routing override for that tenant to eu-pool until DNS converges. I'll open an emergency config change.

kai_eng: Starting rollback now: ```/deploy rollbacks/cname-canary --target api.example.com --revert-to eu-edge --force```

deploy-bot: rollback-job-842 queued by kai_eng. ETA ~45s.

devon_net: I'll contact upstream resolver teams to request clearing of cached CNAME for major ISP blocks; also set short-term 60s TTL on api.example.com A/CNAME to speed convergence.

alex_support: Customer asked for repro steps for their devs: I recommended `dig +trace api.example.com` and `curl -v --resolve api.example.com:443:192.0.2.11 https://api.example.com/health` to confirm landing pop.

alex_support: Also asked them to collect full request/response headers for failed requests and we gave sample script: ```python
import requests
print(requests.get('https://api.example.com/endpoint', headers={'Authorization':'Bearer ...'}).headers)
```

maria_sre: After rollback completes we'll monitor for 30m. If we still see apac answers from EU IPs, escalate to DNS provider for cache purge and coordinate with ISPs.

kai_eng: Root cause notes for postmortem: missing automated revert step for canary CNAME + aggressive cached responses from upstream resolvers + ECS/EDNS behaviors; regional token validation coupling made auth brittle.

tony_pm: Action items assigned: kai -> postmortem draft, devon -> ISP cache outreach + TTL change, maria -> routing override + monitor, alex -> customer comms and advise on token validation fallback.

alex_support: Customer notified: we deployed rollback and route override, asked them to flush caches and send headers if they still hit apac. Thanks all. :pray:

maria_sre: Monitoring: seeing EU client IPs back to eu-pool within 90s of rollback. Will keep watch for 30m and post final status. :white_check_mark:
